mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change < -3% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained UNRATE increases > 0.3pp for three months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by > 1% for four consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in RSAFS (consumer savings) by more than 2% signals a tightening monetary environment with reduced household liquidity, which depresses consumer spending and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND RSAFS falls by > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and RSAFS falls by > 2% in the same month (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% from the previous month signals a robust residential investment cycle, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST rises by > 10% month-over-month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above 0.4 percentage points indicates a labor market expansion with slack, which boosts consumer purchasing power and corporate hiring, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises > 0.4pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise by > 0.4pp in the same month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which prompts anticipatory monetary tightening and erodes corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY for six consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).
